words.ex: The school director said yes to our class's request for a longer lunch break on hot days.
You need a letter of permission from your parents to go on the school trip to the zoo.
My cousin's suggestion was to take the night train to Bukhara, and nobody had a better plan.
Excuse me, could you possibly move your bag so that I can sit down?
Mum phoned our neighbour: 'Hello, Mrs Rahimova, I wonder if you could water our plants while we're in Fergana?'
alt: I was wondering if you could

words.ex: 'Can you lend me your calculator?' 'Sorry, I'm afraid I can't; I need it for my own test.'
'Could you help me carry these boxes up to the fourth floor?' 'Yes, of course!'
'These apples look delicious.' 'Please help yourself to another one. Eat as many as you want!'
'Can I try your new bike?' 'Sure, go ahead and ride it round the yard, but be careful at the corner.'
Before the exam started, Bekzod put up his hand and asked, 'May I borrow a pencil?' 'Yes, you may,' said the teacher.
I was ill yesterday; can I have a look at your notes from the history lesson before the test?
In the dentist's waiting room, a woman asked me, 'Excuse me, do you mind if I charge my phone here?' 'No, not at all.'
The rain has stopped at last. Where shall we go this afternoon, the park or the zoo?
I'm tired of staying indoors all day, so let's go for a walk along the Ankhor canal, shall we?
'What can we do if it rains on Saturday?' 'Well, we could always visit the museum instead of playing football in the park.'
'I don't know what to buy Malika for her birthday.' 'Well, how about getting her a new sketchbook? She loves drawing.'
The queue for the cable car is huge, so why don't we come back early tomorrow morning?
My brother called from the stadium: 'I've got two free tickets, so do you fancy watching the match with me?'
'Shall we eat at home tonight or go out?' 'Honestly, I don't mind; you choose.'
When Laylo suggested a picnic in the botanical garden, everyone said it was a great idea.
'Can we take the old road over the hills?' 'Yes, if you like, but it's much slower.'
'We could meet at the Registan at six.' 'That sounds good; see you there.'
'Let's walk all the way home.' 'Hmm, I don't fancy that; it's nearly five kilometres.'

words.uz: Men … ni afzal ko‘raman (… dan ko‘ra)
words.ex: 'Shall we take the bus to the market?' 'Mm, I'd rather walk than stand on a crowded bus.'
'Can you pass me that pen?' 'Sure, here you are.'
At the bus stop, an old man asked me, 'Could you read this timetable for me, please? I've left my glasses at home.'
Excuse me, could I possibly use your phone? Mine has no battery.
'Which film shall we watch tonight?' 'Honestly, I'm happy with anything, so you choose.'
